sendgrid:index/eventWebhook:EventWebhook.description: Manages SendGrid Event Webhook settings. Event Webhooks allow you to receive real-time notifications about email events such as deliveries, opens, clicks, bounces, and more. Multiple webhooks can be created per account. **Important Notes:** - There is only one event webhook per SendGrid account (or subuser) - The webhook cannot be deleted, only disabled - Event types require specific tracking settings to be enabled: - `open` and `click` events require Open Tracking and Click Tracking - `unsubscribe`, `groupResubscribe`, and `groupUnsubscribe` require Subscription Tracking - Use `friendlyName` to help identify your webhook (available in SendGrid dashboard) - OAuth authentication is optional but recommended for enhanced security - Signature verification can be enabled for webhook request verification ## Example Usage ```typescript import * as pulumi from "@pulumi/pulumi"; import * as sendgrid from "@nellisauction/pulumi-sendgrid"; // Basic event webhook configuration const basic = new sendgrid.EventWebhook("basic", { enabled: true, url: "https://api.myapp.com/sendgrid/events", friendlyName: "Production Event Webhook", delivered: true, bounce: true, dropped: true, spamReport: true, unsubscribe: true, open: true, click: true, processed: true, deferred: true, groupResubscribe: true, groupUnsubscribe: true, }); // Multiple webhooks example const dev = new sendgrid.EventWebhook("dev", { enabled: true, url: "https://dev.myapp.com/sendgrid/events", friendlyName: "Development Webhook", delivered: true, bounce: true, dropped: true, }); const prod = new sendgrid.EventWebhook("prod", { enabled: true, url: "https://prod.myapp.com/sendgrid/events", friendlyName: "Production Webhook", delivered: true, bounce: true, dropped: true, spamReport: true, open: true, click: true, }); ``` ```python import pulumi import pulumi_sendgrid as sendgrid # Basic event webhook configuration basic = sendgrid.EventWebhook("basic", enabled=True, url="https://api.myapp.com/sendgrid/events", friendly_name="Production Event Webhook", delivered=True, bounce=True, dropped=True, spam_report=True, unsubscribe=True, open=True, click=True, processed=True, deferred=True, group_resubscribe=True, group_unsubscribe=True) # Multiple webhooks example dev = sendgrid.EventWebhook("dev", enabled=True, url="https://dev.myapp.com/sendgrid/events", friendly_name="Development Webhook", delivered=True, bounce=True, dropped=True) prod = sendgrid.EventWebhook("prod", enabled=True, url="https://prod.myapp.com/sendgrid/events", friendly_name="Production Webhook", delivered=True, bounce=True, dropped=True, spam_report=True, open=True, click=True) ``` ```csharp using System.Collections.Generic; using System.Linq; using Pulumi; using SendGrid = Pulumi.SendGrid; return await Deployment.RunAsync(() => { // Basic event webhook configuration var basic = new SendGrid.EventWebhook("basic", new() { Enabled = true, Url = "https://api.myapp.com/sendgrid/events", FriendlyName = "Production Event Webhook", Delivered = true, Bounce = true, Dropped = true, SpamReport = true, Unsubscribe = true, Open = true, Click = true, Processed = true, Deferred = true, GroupResubscribe = true, GroupUnsubscribe = true, }); // Multiple webhooks example var dev = new SendGrid.EventWebhook("dev", new() { Enabled = true, Url = "https://dev.myapp.com/sendgrid/events", FriendlyName = "Development Webhook", Delivered = true, Bounce = true, Dropped = true, }); var prod = new SendGrid.EventWebhook("prod", new() { Enabled = true, Url = "https://prod.myapp.com/sendgrid/events", FriendlyName = "Production Webhook", Delivered = true, Bounce = true, Dropped = true, SpamReport = true, Open = true, Click = true, }); }); ``` ```go package main import ( "github.com/nellisauction/pulumi-sendgrid/sdk/go/sendgrid" "github.com/pulumi/pulumi/sdk/v3/go/pulumi" ) func main() { pulumi.Run(func(ctx *pulumi.Context) error { // Basic event webhook configuration _, err := sendgrid.NewEventWebhook(ctx, "basic", &sendgrid.EventWebhookArgs{ Enabled: pulumi.Bool(true), Url: pulumi.String("https://api.myapp.com/sendgrid/events"), FriendlyName: pulumi.String("Production Event Webhook"), Delivered: pulumi.Bool(true), Bounce: pulumi.Bool(true), Dropped: pulumi.Bool(true), SpamReport: pulumi.Bool(true), Unsubscribe: pulumi.Bool(true), Open: pulumi.Bool(true), Click: pulumi.Bool(true), Processed: pulumi.Bool(true), Deferred: pulumi.Bool(true), GroupResubscribe: pulumi.Bool(true), GroupUnsubscribe: pulumi.Bool(true), }) if err != nil { return err } // Multiple webhooks example _, err = sendgrid.NewEventWebhook(ctx, "dev", &sendgrid.EventWebhookArgs{ Enabled: pulumi.Bool(true), Url: pulumi.String("https://dev.myapp.com/sendgrid/events"), FriendlyName: pulumi.String("Development Webhook"), Delivered: pulumi.Bool(true), Bounce: pulumi.Bool(true), Dropped: pulumi.Bool(true), }) if err != nil { return err } _, err = sendgrid.NewEventWebhook(ctx, "prod", &sendgrid.EventWebhookArgs{ Enabled: pulumi.Bool(true), Url: pulumi.String("https://prod.myapp.com/sendgrid/events"), FriendlyName: pulumi.String("Production Webhook"), Delivered: pulumi.Bool(true), Bounce: pulumi.Bool(true), Dropped: pulumi.Bool(true), SpamReport: pulumi.Bool(true), Open: pulumi.Bool(true), Click: .groupResubscribe(true) .groupUnsubscribe(true) .build()); // Multiple webhooks example var dev = new EventWebhook("dev", EventWebhookArgs.builder() .enabled(true) .url("https://dev.myapp.com/sendgrid/events") .friendlyName("Development Webhook") .delivered(true) .bounce(true) .dropped(true) .build()); var prod = new EventWebhook("prod", EventWebhookArgs.builder() .enabled(true) .url("https://prod.myapp.com/sendgrid/events") .friendlyName("Production Webhook") .delivered(true) .bounce(true) .dropped(true) .spamReport(true) .open(true) .click(true) .build()); } } ``` ```yaml resources: # Basic event webhook configuration basic: type: sendgrid:EventWebhook properties: enabled: true url: https://api.myapp.com/sendgrid/events friendlyName: Production Event Webhook delivered: true bounce: true dropped: true spamReport: true unsubscribe: true # Engagement events (requires tracking enabled) open: true click: true # Processing events processed: true deferred: true # Group events (requires subscription tracking) groupResubscribe: true groupUnsubscribe: true # Multiple webhooks example dev: type: sendgrid:EventWebhook properties: enabled: true url: https://dev.myapp.com/sendgrid/events friendlyName: Development Webhook delivered: true bounce: true dropped: true prod: type: sendgrid:EventWebhook properties: enabled: true url: https://prod.myapp.com/sendgrid/events friendlyName: Production Webhook delivered: true bounce: true dropped: true spamReport: true open: true click: true ``` ## Additional Information ### Event Types The following event types are available: - **delivered**: Message successfully delivered to receiving server - **processed**: Message received by SendGrid and ready for delivery - **dropped**: Message not delivered (spam, invalid address, etc.) - **deferred**: Recipient's email server temporarily rejected message - **bounce**: Receiving server permanently rejected message - **open**: Recipient opened the HTML message (requires Open Tracking) - **click**: Recipient clicked a link (requires Click Tracking) - **spam_report**: Recipient marked message as spam - **unsubscribe**: Recipient clicked subscription management link - **group_unsubscribe**: Recipient unsubscribed from specific group - **group_resubscribe**: Recipient resubscribed to specific group ### Security For enhanced security, you can: 1. Enable OAuth authentication by providing `oauthClientId`, `oauthClientSecret`, and `oauthTokenUrl` 2. Enable signature verification using the `signed` field 3. Use the `publicKey` (computed) for webhook payload verification ### References - [SendGrid Event Webhook Documentation](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/create-an-event-webhook) - [Event Webhook Overview](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/for-developers/tracking-events/event)

sendgrid:index/ssoCertificate:SsoCertifi.description:
## Example Usage

## Import

The `pulumi import` command can be used, for example:

!/bin/bash

Import SSO certificate using its ID

```sh
$ pulumi import sendgrid:index/ssoCertificate:SsoCertificate okta_cert cert-1234-5678
```

Find certificate IDs in SendGrid dashboard under Settings > SSO > Certificates

integrationId.description: An ID that matches an existing SSO integration.

publicCertificate.description:
This public certificate allows SendGrid to verify that
				SAML requests it receives are signed by an IdP that it recognizes.

This public certificate allows SendGrid to verify that

integrationId.description: An ID that matches an existing SSO integration.

publicCertificate.description:
This public certificate allows SendGrid to verify that
				SAML requests it receives are signed by an IdP that it recognizes.

audienceUrl.description:
The URL where your IdP should POST its SAML response.
				This is the Twilio SendGrid URL that is responsible for receiving and parsing a SAML assertion.
				This is the same URL as the Single Sign-On URL when using SendGrid.

completedIntegration.description: Indicates if the integration is complete.

enabled.description: Indicates if the integration is enabled.

entityId.description:
An identifier provided by your IdP to identify Twilio SendGrid in the SAML interaction.
				This is called the 'SAML Issuer ID' in the Twilio SendGrid UI.

name.description: The name of the integration.

signinUrl.description:
The IdP's SAML POST endpoint. This endpoint should receive requests
				and initiate an SSO login flow. This is called the 'Embed Link' in the Twilio SendGrid UI.

signoutUrl.description:
This URL is relevant only for an IdP-initiated authentication flow.
				If a user authenticates from their IdP, this URL will return them to their IdP when logging out.

singleSignonUrl.description:
The URL where your IdP should POST its SAML response.
				This is the Twilio SendGrid URL that is responsible for receiving and parsing a SAML assertion.
				This is the same URL as the Audience URL when using SendGrid.

enabled.description: Indicates if the integration is enabled.

entityId.description:
An identifier provided by your IdP to identify Twilio SendGrid in the SAML interaction.
				This is called the 'SAML Issuer ID' in the Twilio SendGrid UI.

name.description: The name of the integration.

signinUrl.description:
The IdP's SAML POST endpoint. This endpoint should receive requests
				and initiate an SSO login flow. This is called the 'Embed Link' in the Twilio SendGrid UI.

signoutUrl.description:
This URL is relevant only for an IdP-initiated authentication flow.
				If a user authenticates from their IdP, this URL will return them to their IdP when logging out.

email.description: The email address of the teammate. This will be used as the teammate's login.

firstName.description: The first name of the teammate. Required for SSO users.

isAdmin.description: Whether the teammate should have admin privileges. Admin teammates have full access to the account and don't need specific scopes.

isSso.description: Whether this is a Single Sign-On (SSO) user. SSO users require first*name and last*name.

lastName.description: The last name of the teammate. Required for SSO users.

scopes.description: List of permission scopes for the teammate. Ignored if is*admin is true. Cannot include '2fa*exempt' or '2fa*required' as these are managed automatically by SendGrid. This attribute is also computed: leaving it unset keeps whatever scopes the teammate currently has on the server instead of clearing them, and it must be left unset for a teammate with subuser*access, because SendGrid refuses root scopes for those teammates. See SendGrid API documentation for available scopes.

subuserAccesses.description: Subuser permission grants for this SSO teammate. Only applies when `isSso = true`. Setting at least one block sets `hasRestrictedSubuserAccess = true` on the API. This attribute is also computed: when no block is managed it reflects the teammate's current server-side access without producing a diff, and removing all blocks falls back to that server value rather than clearing access (Terraform does not clobber access it does not manage).

userStatus.description: The status of the user: 'active' for confirmed users, 'pending' for users who haven't accepted their invitation yet.

username.description: The username for the teammate. If not provided, the email will be used.
